free_tier.stated: 'Expose HTTP, TCP, and UDP services from private networks through outbound WireGuard tunnels. Keep control of your public endpoint, routing, certificates, and access policies.' The software is self-hosted; no vendor plan and no vendor quota.

egress.terms: No allowance is published because there is no vendor in the path: the server's NIC and its hosting bill are the limit.; ingress: tcp+udp

record.tooling: wiredoor CLI, Docker, the server dashboard
record.chaining: runs on the same free-tier VPS as Pangolin or Wireport, so the three are alternatives rather than additions; the VPS egress is the shared ceiling

limits.value: the software imposes no byte meter; what runs out is the monthly allowance of the host it runs on, and that host is a separate provider

record.binding_note: the software imposes no byte meter; what runs out is the monthly allowance of the host it runs on, and that host is a separate provider

identity_cost.detail: Self-hosted: the only account is the local admin the installer creates ('username: admin@example.com'). No vendor registration.

record.reliability_note: the public endpoint is the operator's; its uptime, certificate renewal and firewall are all local work
record.confidence_note: WireGuard tunnel proxy architecture and relay routing are documented in repository specifications.

evidence.proved: 'Expose HTTP, TCP, and UDP services from private networks through outbound WireGuard tunnels'; 'Route web applications by domain or path and TCP or UDP services by an approved public port'
'Wiredoor assign unused port automatically in the range defined by TCP_SERVICES_PORT_RANGE', via the search index snippet

record.notes: The second half of the ingress chain is missing: Wiredoor Server must sit on a host with a public IP. It is software, not a service, so the free tier is the VPS, not Wiredoor. The FAQ page was read through the search index rather than a direct fetch, which is why its evidence row is weaker than the home page.

extras.wg_detail: 'Remote nodes connect outward to Wiredoor Server, and forwarded traffic crosses the encrypted tunnel.' The wiredoor CLI or the dashboard token holds the tunnel; no .conf export is documented.
extras.volume_stated: No allowance is published because there is no vendor in the path: the server's NIC and its hosting bill are the limit.
extras.transit_note: the server receives on its public port and forwards down the outbound WireGuard tunnel to the private node
